title: The Bosphorus Brief — Monday, 21 September 2026
overview: Regional tension is the story of the day: Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and sharp US-Iran rhetoric are pulling in Ankara, which has offered Riyadh military support. At home, the lira's slide continues, a bank license revocation is making headlines, and Turkey faces fresh Council of Europe deadlines on rights cases. None of this changes daily logistics dramatically, but it's worth watching your bank and your euro/dollar conversions this week.
body: Yemen's Houthis have warned of further attacks on Saudi Arabia, and the Houthis have separately declared a "blockade for blockade" against the kingdom while saying US ships remain safe. Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said Turkey is ready to help meet Saudi military needs, particularly in technical areas — a notable step given Ankara's growing defense-export profile. State media (Al Jazeera) and international outlets (Bloomberg, Sky News) are covering the Houthi threat itself; opposition-leaning Turkish Minute is the main source flagging Ankara's specific offer. For residents, this is a diplomatic and economic story for now — no direct travel disruption reported, though the US State Department has issued a security alert tied to broader Iran-US friction, and both Iran and the US are trading warnings about renewed strikes. Worth monitoring if you have Gulf travel plans.
